Transmission-line corridor inspection, sized for a Trinity F90+ class aircraft (17 m/s cruise, ~90 min).

Utilities fly corridors as a long out-and-back rather than a block: the asset is linear, so the flight plan is too. 120 m AGL is the BVLOS ceiling in most of Europe and the US. The outbound imaging run is flown at 14 m/s because ground-sample distance and motion blur set the speed when you are photographing something; the return is a straight transit at 17 m/s with nothing to shoot.

Run it with wind to see why that asymmetry matters. Outbound and return are reciprocal headings, so intuition says the wind should roughly cancel. It does not: an 8 m/s crosswind-on-the-nose takes the SLOW imaging leg from 31 to 72 minutes while the faster return only saves 8, and the whole flight goes from 62 to 97 minutes. A headwind hurts most on the leg you are already flying slowly. The mission still completes on this aircraft, but with the reserve margin down from 54 Wh to 21 Wh.
